Description: after this efa77533053f663458feb0931b1e5f36c2b96e80
was delivered we changed the logic of detecting old SN packets,
and relied on FW to tell the driver when the SN is old, looks like
the FW is not indicating this correctly in
the packet we receive.
which resulted in TPUT degradation in OPEN TCP connection
since we forwarded old packets to the OS TCP stack.
in secured connection there is no TPUT issue since the old packets
are dropped due to PN check for REPLAY ATTACK after the re-order
buffer phase and hence not forwarding it to the OS.
in UDP there is no degradation also since there is no congestion
control in UDP
the solution is to check the newly arrived sequence if it is
old sequence and to drop it in old sn check
we also added a check on the newNormSsn position related
to the reorder window, and if it is outside it
we move the window accordignly

column4: [Lenovo Thinkpad JP][Alderlake][Jaguar2/Panther2][GarfieldPeak2][Win10/Win11] 11ac-5Ghz Wifi performance is lower in DC mode compared to AC mode when using Netgear R9000 AP model
column34:
AP sends rts to wake station and cause open 2 antennas, STA sends CTS
AP sends first aggregation and CTS to self  in order not allow medium
to move to idle and keep 2 antennas ready before sending next aggregation
The bug is that in Solar L2P doesn't set L2P_GCSR_STAT_SE_CTRL_PENDING_MSK bit at MH parsing
for CTRL frames that not for us, and when we recevie CTRL frame not for us in solar we don't path
thought regular ctlr frame flow that allows to delay the air protection time and allow to receive the next RX MIMO frame before 1 antenna is closed
in solar we just update nav, and dump CTRL frames not for us
the fix is to add the same logic as in regular CTRL frames flow in solar nad add air protection delay if required (DSMPS)

column4: [Lenovo-IdeaPad][Inhouse][S540-13][CML][JFP2][20H1][SS]Disconnect from AP when playing online video
column34:
Debug has shown the INA controllers become stuck in illegal state, in which there can be no preamble detections until the RX is reset. This happens when packets are received in high input power and the receiver is reset while such packet is still on air.

We traced the cause to a combination of INA HW bug and a long-existing FW workaround:

There’s a config register called CCK_PURE_11B which disables the OFDM preamble detector. It was originally intended to be used with APs that support CCK only without OFDM. Since it was considered an esoteric feature it was not thoroughly validated.
Due to HW bug, if CCK_PURE_11B=1 and there’s high incoming power which leads to AGC Fast Step, it’s possible for the preamble detection module to remain turned off when it’s supposed to turn on. Whether that happens depends on relative phase between 2 clock signals when entering a specific state of the controller FSM. Having the preamble detector turned off instead of on prevents detection, and it also prevent restoring the gain to max since the controller waits for the detector to indicate that preamble wasn’t found. It’s only possible to exist this state by toggling rx_en, or if CCK detection is not required as in HB.

column34:
This issue only occurs on HE connection due to HTC support bit in HE MAC capabilities.
Galaxy S10 decides to turn on the 'Order Flag' bit in the DHCP frame control flags due to this bit.
This bit means that the MAC header has 4 additional bytes of HT Control (HTC).
The LLC comes right after the MAC header in the packet.
The OS complains that the LLC is invalid, even tho in pass/fail cases the LLC is the same.
If we remove the additional 4 bytes of HTC the connection succeeds.

Therefore this seems to be like an OS issue which is not taking the extra 4 bytes into consideration, thus dropping the DHCP request and not sending a DHCP reply for the driver to send.

As a temporal fix, disable the HTC supported bit in HE MAC capabilities for softAP/GO.

Root cause:

AP send Addba request and imeddiatelly after that M1 EAPOL (SN0)
Driver receive addba request and starting to open aggregation with FW and send Addba response
When driver receive first EAPOL (M1) the open aggregation flow doesn't finished, and driver handle M1 as normal packet (not AGG) 
driver send to AP M2 EAPOL, and AP send to driver M3 (SN1)
when driver receive M3, the Open aggregation flow already finished, and driver store M3 (SN1) in reorder buffer (SN0 is missing in reorder buffer, because was handled as normal packet)
second after that AP send new M3 (SN2), driver see that packet SN1 is aged, and notify to OS 2 M3 packets
OS answer to first of them with M4, but AP expect to M4 for second M2


The Fix: Upon connection establishment (encryption ready), answer ADDBA response with decline status, and only after connect aggree to aggregation

column4: [Lenovo-IdeaPad][Inhouse][KBL-R][Yoga930][RS5]WiFi icon shows limited connection after resume from MS, but it can auto recover in 30~60secs
column34:
When D3 flow starts, driver does not close RX
aggregations. D0 (FW) code doesn't close them as well, but D3
code sends DELBA frame to AP (on all opened TIDs). This actually
tells AP that we close all recipient aggregations, but DRV and D0 code
remain in the 'old' state, where aggregations are still open.
The problem starts when we move back to D0. For DRV after resuming
from D3 AP will try another ADDBA on an existing TID, when FW D0
code runs still with open aggregation window and AP sends single frames
or aggregated frames out-of-window, so it may case FW some
inconsistency on the BACK window and probably to 'loose' these
frames
the idea of the fix is to close all opened aggregation internally.
Note: UT is being implemented, one test with suspend/resume was
tested manually and passed.

column34:
WDI RX flush CB is sent via job.
A mutual deadlock was found in RX flush flow when miniport reset and WDI RX flush are running in parallel cores. In this flow, one core is in the middle of miniport reset and waits for all DPCs to end rvIsrWaitForAllActiveDpcsToEnd). The other core is running DPC DPC (ECHO_RSP RX) calling RxFlushConfirm. This indication goes to WDI which stalls (CompletePendingCancelSendsOrHaltJobs) and waits for the reset to complete causing a mutual deadlock for two cores waiting one for each other.

column34:
Peer removal while internal TX
Peer can be removed after classification is done, prior to addition into the TID Q. This flow is not guarded correctly and therefore, can happen especially for internal data TX, which is mostly used by AMT. In case of external packet, IRQL is raised in order to protect peer removal on same core, though, can still happen on parallel core.

The fix is to minimize the time between the classification and the addition in to the TID Q. Once packet is inserted into the TID Q, peer removal is protected. There is no logical change besides pushing the classification to the edge of the insert into the TID Q.

column34:
Reconfigure LQ after resuming from D3
When resume from D3 is complete, there is a need to reconfigure (reset) LQ. Currently LQ "reconfigure" flow is distributed among all the VIFs, bound to several events and doesn't have a single flow.
The correct place is probably to do it from DP MAC reconfigure, however, this change cannot be currently done in the scope of a bug fix.
After resuming from (connected) D3 there is no LQ reconfigure and it is assumed that TLC will converge based on TX responses.
Statistics collector ignores all TX responses, since belonging to older 'color' (rateTableID) preventing from TLC to upscale and open AGG.
The result is basic rates in TX, no AGGs and long pings.

The fix is to unset the lowest rates which were set during D3 entering flow without resetting station's LQ.
The reason not to reset is since no LQ command can be sent anyway so need to wait to TLC convergence based on TX responses.

column34:
WDI: max supported SGLs (per NBL), use 19 instead of 8
Current capability to WDI is to support up to 8 SGLs per NBL.
This value is hardcoded, since 'normal' NBLs should not have more than this value.
However, in case of LSO, we can exceed it, since we support up to 32 KB LSO size, where each SGL is limited to page size (4 KB). 
In such case, where NBL has more than 8 SGLs, WDI will drop it. (it will try to 'fix' it, and might fail).

The fix for CC30 is to enlarge this value to 19 (MAX_TBs - 1). The maximal NBL which we can transmit (in case we do not copy it) can contain 19 SGLs.
This is a HW limitation (ThP and below) for the TX command. TBs array has 20 entries.

The fix for main will have different logic: driver will not limit this value and will be support up to 0xFFFF (infinity).
In case we are getting NBL with more than MAX_TBs - 1 SGLs, driver will drop it (or copy). In such way, the drop will be monitored and visible.

BCN/PROBE handling (in noisy environment) in DPC causing jitters/noise in audio due to long DPC time (~15 ms). 
DPC chop is not enough, since current limits are 20 ms for weak CPU. Reducing DPC chop time even more, will harm TpT.

The fix is to move handling into a different core, and free the main core (0).
This is done by triggering work item, which will raise IRQL back to DPC.
Need to consider moving BCN/PROBE parsing into work item in passive IRQL (not part of this delivery).

column4: CLONE - [Lenovo ThinkPad JP][Thames2/LnL/FmP][QS][PCIe] BT Device lost due to TOP exception during S4 cycle - Clean WA from FW/Driver to retrieve debug
column34:
While executing a D3 scenario, prior to entering D0, we observed incorrect PCIE context info, which we suspect is due to an unidentified bug in the hardware. Consequently, the firmware (FW) triggered a fatal exception, leading to a soft reset of the CPU. During this soft reset, we encountered an additional Top exception rewriting all original exception data that was alraedy recorded in persistent.

The details of this Top exception suggest an issue that occurred during the initialization of the FSEQ following the soft reset due to original exception. However, the extra details provided by the Top exception data was inconclusive as per Top team. We assume that the hardware may have already been in a bad state due to the original issue when FW attempted to program the FSEQ as part of the initialization after the soft reset.

Due to the current exception handling approach, we lacked adequate data for debugging.

Proposed Solution: To address this issue, systems suggested halting the CPU immediately after any exception occurs. This will allow the host to collect debug information related to the exception before the firmware proceeds further and trigger further exceptions due to any instability already in the system.

column4: [Lenovo ThinkPad JP][LCFC][Drift3/Ironhide3][TGL][CCP][20H2]Three new HLK Bluetooth test items appear in Win10 20H2 after installing Tile
column34:
Problem statement: As part of system preparation using sysprep.exe and generalization in Windows Audit mode, the Bluetooth driver resulted in YB.

Background: The Intel Tile Node is a raw PDO that exposes interface for Tile application to send request to Driver though IO CTL interface. The raw PDO will appear as hidden device in Device manager under Other devices section without any device properties. OEMs raised a concern about the new node also requested to populate device properties for this node to adopt in the OEM Automation / testing. As part of adding the Device Properties for Tile Node, the Intel Tile Node device is made as child device for Bluetooth driver node to inherit all the properties of Parent. To achieve this, ibtusb.inf is modified to represent Tile Node as Null Device and child of Intel Bluetooth Driver.

Analysis: As part of Driver installation using MSI, the package will install all the drivers that are included in it . This is a PNP installation requirement to support Plug and Play of devices. The MSI will install all the driver including CcP and HrP which contains the Tile Node INF entries though the platform having TyP connected. The Driver will included the firmware for respective SKUs only. After Installation in audit mode and then performing Generalization, It is observed that Windows OS is loading different SKU driver Binary ( in this case it is CCP) where the TyP firmware will not be present. Due to this, the driver will result in Yellow Bang. This has been confirmed form the driver logs.

This has been narrowed down further by uninstalling the CcP and HrP SKU drivers manually after installation and then performing the Generalization in audit mode. In this case, the Windows OS is loading the driver Binary for the respective SKUs.
Few more points:
- Bluetooth Driver name (ibtusb.sys) and INF(ibtusb.inf) is same for all SKUs .
- The Intel Tile Node INF Entries are present only in HrP and CcP. These drivers are installed as part of MSI package and which binds the Tile node with ibtusb.sys/ibtusb.inf ( Additional clarification required here from MSFT )
- The issue is narrowed down only. However, the root cause of the issue still need to be investigated based on feedback from MSFT. We have Open sighting with MSFT PnP team on this (https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16012307683 ).

Test Coverage: As part of Test coverage, all the testing including the installation is performed in Normal windows mode. Switching between Normal OS to Audit mode and then Generalization is not covered. This is the process followed in Factories for imaging the platforms. This is the gap identified and is required to add testing coverage in Install domain areas.

column34:
WHQL failures reported in this Issue are due to FW watchdog exceptions. One of the LE Scan transaction has corrupted endTransaction native slot programmed, which caused all subsequent jobs to be incorrectly programmed. When this happens, LC scheduler will not be able program BC layer and start a job, and just keep running LC Preprocessor forever until WD exception occurs.

LE scans are of 37ms window size. If controller gets a sync within this window, then LC scheduler will try to program another LE Scan window for the time remaining in the 37ms window.
It looks like the issue (incorrect end native slot) happens while programming the second LE scan window. when very little scan window is left for the second scan transaction

Fix:
As we know that the endTransaction native slot is getting corrupted, a check is added if the duration of the Current Job is greater than 100ms then the Job is cancelled and preprocessor is called which will schedule the next job based on the current native slot instead of the corrupted endTransaction native slot.
